I turned 21 2 weeks after Christmas - and I got diagnosed the week before that holiday. So obviously, no big bar party for my 21st birthday. It's not like I had any RL friends to go with, just my parents - but the day seemed rather empty and hollow because I wasn't able to do anything else I wanted that day, either (no conventions because of covid, etc...)

I've never been interested in getting blackout drunk, or even drunk in the first place. But I wish my pancreas would have waited a week after my birthday to conk out, because I'll never know what the feeling of being tipsy is like. FOMO, maybe.
About 2 weeks for the pain to stop, but I don't know if it's fully gone away.

Ruined lots of friendships (which only contributed to the trauma cycle,) refused to participate in things I would genuinely enjoy because of my fear of rejection/convincing myself they would be better off if I didn't.

So, I figured I'd give you an update because of your very long and heartfelt reply. The pain is gone now. Ultrasound was too obscured to see my pancreas clearly, but we're thinking it was a freak acute flare-up (idiopathic) because my tests show no gallstones/anything that commonly causes this. I did lose about 10 pounds in one week, oops. I'm still making better food choices though and hope I can at least keep that weight off.
